QF.id: XXVA Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards_8

question.text: According to the workbook, the qualities of a good research analyst include:

answer.text: Being negative about all investment opportunities
Being methodical, having an enquiring mind, asking pertinent questions, cross-verifying management claims, and evaluating information rigorously before making recommendations
Accepting all company management claims at face value
Refusing to cover any company that has ever had regulatory issues

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes a good research analyst as someone with a methodical and enquiring/discerning mind, who asks pertinent questions, pays attention to detail, cross-verifies management claims and conducts rigorous research with unbiased evaluation of assumptions before reaching conclusions. The Trap: Being negative on every opportunity, accepting management claims at face value or refusing to cover companies with past regulatory issues all contradict the source-described approach of careful, evidence-based analysis. Note: The wording mirrors the workbook's qualities of an RA; the term professional skepticism is avoided since it was not found in the pages checked.
